issues: lib/letflow/design/req192-service-catalog-routes.md section 5: the claim 'reading it via Ecto.Query/Repo.all/1 from a router is not different in kind from Letflow.Routers.Audit's or Letflow.Routers.Metrics's own direct-schema-query precedents' is FALSE on inspection. lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex delegates to Letflow.EventStore.read_global/1 (a context-module function); lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex delegates to Letflow.Engine.count_instances_by_status/1 etc (also context-module functions). Neither queries a schema directly. grep -rln 'Ecto.Query|Repo\.(all|one|get)' lib/letflow/routers/ matches only a comment in promotions.ex mentioning Ecto.Query.CastError -- no actual direct-schema-query call exists anywhere under lib/letflow/routers/ today. This is a fabricated precedent used to justify a real, first-of-its-kind exception to this codebase's router->context-module layering discipline. Fix: remove the false Audit/Metrics precedent claim; state plainly that GET /admin/services querying Entry directly is a genuine layering exception made necessary only because REQ-192's scope forbids a service_catalog.ex change and AC2 cannot otherwise be satisfied, and flag it explicitly for REVIEWER sign-off at Step 2d rather than folding it into 'consistent with existing precedent.' The underlying decision to query Entry directly does not need to be reversed -- only its stated justification does.
result.verdict_statement: FAIL. Section 5 asserts a direct-schema-query precedent in Letflow.Routers.Audit/Letflow.Routers.Metrics that does not exist in the real source -- both routers delegate to context-module functions, and no router under lib/letflow/routers/ queries a schema directly today. Everything else checked (two-router claim, permission mapping, 409 constructor shape, both field-gap findings, the stale-comment finding, no fenced code) is accurate and unambiguous. Full detail in handoffs/WF02-REQ192-20260830/req192-design-validation-report.md.
